flashcards.front: GuardDuty generates a finding 'Recon:EC2/PortProbeUnprotectedPort' for multiple ?
flashcards.back: GuardDuty does not natively isolate instances. The standard automated remediation pattern uses EventBridge to match specific GuardDuty finding types and trigger Lambda functions. The Lambda uses EC2 API to modify instance security group associations. EventBridge rule patterns can filter by finding type, severity, and affected resource to target responses precisely. trigger a Lambda function that removes the instance from its security group and attaches the quarantine security group

flashcards.front: A security engineer needs to investigate a potential security incident involving?
flashcards.back: Amazon Detective automatically ingests and correlates data from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty findings to create behavior graphs. It allows investigators to visualize API activity timelines, geolocation of IP addresses, IAM entity behavior profiles, and relationships between resources — all without requiring manual CloudTrail queries. It's specifically designed for security investigation workflows. VPC Flow Logs, and GuardDuty findings to build entity behavior profiles and visualize activity timelines

flashcards.front: A company is experiencing a suspected DDoS attack targeting its web application ?
flashcards.back: AWS Shield Advanced provides: 24/7 access to the AWS DDoS Response Team (DRT) for active attack assistance, DDoS cost protection (credits for scaling costs during attacks), advanced metrics and reporting per protected resource, and automatic application layer attack detection with WAF rule auto-creation. Shield Standard only provides automatic protection against common layer 3/4 attacks without these additional features. which provides DDoS cost protection credits, proactive engagement from the DRT, and enhanced detection for specific resources

flashcards.front: A security team receives a GuardDuty finding 'UnauthorizedAccess:IAMUser/Console?
flashcards.back: The recommended investigation flow: (1) Use the GuardDuty finding to identify the IAM principal and source IP, (2) Query CloudTrail for all API calls by that principal after the suspicious login time, (3) Use Amazon Detective to visualize the entity's behavior graph — it correlates CloudTrail events, shows IP geolocation, resource access patterns, and peer comparison against historical baseline. Detective significantly accelerates investigation compared to manual CloudTrail queries. then use Amazon Detective to visualize the full activity timeline and correlated resources

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A company's S3 bucket stores confidential financial records. The security team r?
flashcards.back: S3 Object Lock Compliance mode provides WORM (Write Once, Read Many) protection that cannot be overridden by ANY user including the AWS root account or AWS itself. Objects are immutable until the retention period expires. Compliance mode is specifically designed for regulatory requirements (SEC 17a-4, FINRA, HIPAA) where records must not be altered. Governance mode allows users with s3:BypassGovernanceRetention permission to override the lock. no user, including root, can delete or overwrite objects before the retention period expires

flashcards.front: A security engineer needs to ensure all data stored in an S3 bucket is encrypted?
flashcards.back: A bucket policy with a Deny condition checks the PutObject request headers. The condition 'StringNotEquals: s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms' denies uploads not using SSE-KMS. Adding 'StringNotEquals: s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id: <key-ARN>' further enforces that only the specific CMK is used. Default encryption applies KMS if no header is provided but doesn't reject non-compliant requests — the bucket policy Deny is needed for strict enforcement.

flashcards.front: A company needs to manage TLS certificates for 200 internal microservices using ?
flashcards.back: ACM Private CA (formerly ACM PCA) allows organizations to create a private CA hierarchy and issue private TLS certificates for internal services. Certificates are managed through ACM with automated renewal. Developers can request certificates via ACM API/console without needing access to the CA private key. ACM public certificates require public DNS domain validation and cannot be used for internal-only domains. IAM certificate store doesn't provide issuance or renewal. issue certificates via ACM for internal services with automated renewal

flashcards.front: A KMS customer-managed key (CMK) is used to encrypt S3 data. A security engineer?
flashcards.back: To allow encryption but prevent decryption, grant kms:Encrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey (needed for envelope encryption in S3/SDK) in the KMS key policy, and explicitly Deny kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext. An explicit Deny in the key policy cannot be overridden by identity-based policies. This creates a 'write-only encryption' scenario useful for logging pipelines where the writer should never read back encrypted data.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Amazon Macie is enabled on an S3 bucket containing employee records. Macie gener?
flashcards.back: Macie generates EventBridge events for all sensitive data findings. An EventBridge rule filtering for SensitiveData:S3Object/Personal findings triggers a Lambda that calls s3:GetObjectAcl to check if the object is public, then calls s3:PutObjectAcl to set it private. An SNS notification is sent to the security team. Macie itself only detects, it does not remediate. While S3 Block Public Access is a preventive control, the question asks for automated response to Macie findings. trigger Lambda to check the object ACL and set it to private if public, then send SNS notification

flashcards.front: A company's developer accidentally committed AWS access keys to a public GitHub ?
flashcards.back: When credentials are exposed: immediate deactivation stops ongoing unauthorized use within seconds. Deletion removes the key permanently. CloudTrail allows searching for all API calls made with the specific access key ID (using the accessKeyId filter in CloudTrail Event History) to determine if unauthorized access occurred. GitHub token scanning may have already notified AWS about the exposed key — AWS sometimes auto-deactivates keys it detects on public repos, but don't rely on this. then review CloudTrail for unauthorized activity during the 2-hour exposure window using the compromised access key ID

flashcards.front: A company must ensure that all EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances are encrypt?
flashcards.back: AWS enables 'EBS encryption by default' per region per account — once enabled, any new EBS volume, snapshot, or copy is automatically encrypted with the default KMS key (or a specified CMK). The AWS Config managed rule 'encrypted-volumes' evaluates ALL attached EBS volumes and reports any that are not encrypted, identifying existing non-compliant volumes. Together these controls enforce current and prospective encryption compliance.

flashcards.front: A company uses CloudHSM for storing cryptographic keys. What is the PRIMARY diff?
flashcards.back: KMS is AWS-managed (multi-tenant, FIPS 140-2 Level 2), integrates natively with 100+ AWS services, and AWS has administrative access to key metadata (though not key material for CMKs). CloudHSM is single-tenant dedicated HSM hardware (FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated) in your VPC — AWS has NO access to your keys or HSMs; only your users can access them. CloudHSM is required when: regulatory requirements mandate exclusive key control, Level 3 FIPS validation is required, or custom cryptographic operations are needed. EBS, RDS) while CloudHSM is single-tenant hardware you manage, providing FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validation and exclusive key ownership with no AWS access to your keys

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: A developer needs read access to an S3 bucket in Account B from an EC2 instance ?
flashcards.back: Cross-account S3 access requires BOTH policies to allow: (1) The bucket policy in Account B must grant access to Account A's IAM role, AND (2) The IAM role in Account A must have an identity-based policy allowing s3:GetObject on the specific bucket ARN in Account B. This is different from same-account access where a bucket policy alone can grant access. If either policy denies or doesn't allow, the access fails.

flashcards.front: A company uses Amazon Cognito User Pools for their mobile application authentica?
flashcards.back: Amazon Cognito's AdminUserGlobalSignOut API revokes all valid tokens (ID, access, refresh) for a specific user across all devices and sessions. After calling this API, any request using the user's previous tokens receives an invalid token error. Combined with a forced password reset (AdminSetUserPassword or AdminResetUserPassword), this immediately locks out the compromised account. Token expiry shortening is reactive and doesn't immediately revoke existing tokens. which invalidates all outstanding tokens and refresh tokens for the user across all devices

flashcards.front: A company's security audit finds that IAM users have more permissions than they ?
flashcards.back: IAM Access Advisor (available on every IAM user, role, group, and policy detail page) shows the last time each AWS service was accessed by that entity. For IAM Identity Center permission sets, you can see service last access across accounts. AWS generates 'last accessed' data for service-level and, for some services, action-level granularity. If a service hasn't been accessed in 90 days, the permissions for that service can likely be removed. This data is also available via IAM GetServiceLastAccessedDetails API. which shows the last time each service and action was used by an IAM entity, enabling policy right-sizing

flashcards.front: A company needs to enforce that all S3 buckets created in their accounts use SSE?
flashcards.back: S3 Block Public Access can now be enabled at the AWS Organizations level, automatically applying to all existing and new accounts. An SCP can deny S3 bucket creation without the SSE-KMS header, preventing creation of unencrypted buckets. Config conformance packs deployed via StackSets with automatic deployment cover new accounts automatically. Together these create a zero-touch enforcement layer for all current and future accounts. enable S3 Block Public Access at the organization level via Amazon S3 account settings in Organizations; configure AWS Config conformance packs via StackSets with automatic deployment
